messages:
Liam: Heads up — we just saw a weird routing pattern: a bunch of EU customers got sent to us-east endpoints for ~3m, spikes in p95 and egress. GeoDNS failover fired.
Maya: saw it. Are probes from eu-west failing or is the GeoDNS healthcheck oversensitive? :thinking:
Sophia: infra-bot shows probe flap at 1779991200 -> 1779991260. Logs: `healthcheck: 502 /connect timeout` from two EU LB nodes.
Arjun: could be a transient control-plane flakiness, but also noticed NAT port exhaustion alerts on the EU egress NAT pool at the same time. When NATs saturate, connections collapse and DNS clients pick another region.
Liam: ohhh NAT exhaustion would explain both the 502s and the GeoDNS fallback. Any sign of long-lived connections from batching or hanging KV-caches?
Maya: yes, some LLM-serving pods in eu-west had continuous streaming sessions pinned to a small set of NAT IPs. No adaptive port reuse. We had 1.2x normal streaming concurrency.
Sophia: quick mitigation: increased EU NAT pool by +50 ips and forced LB drain on the smallest outlier hosts. Rolling restart of the offending streaming pods in eu-west helped.
Liam: changed GeoDNS failover policy from strict_health -> prefer_same_continent for 15m window. Also raised DNS TTL from 30 -> 60s to reduce churn while we stabilise.
Arjun: note: increasing TTL reduces churn but makes failover slower if eu actually goes down. For this incident prefer_same_continent seems safer than cross-continent fallback for latency-sensitive requests.
Sophia: opened a follow-up to add NAT port metrics to the per-route console (token-level egress breakdown) and an alert when NAT utilization > 70% for >2m.
Maya: propose a long-term fix: client-side connection multiplexing controls + enforcement of idle timeouts to prevent streaming sessions from hogging NAT ports. Also consider adding ephemeral egress gateways per-availability-zone.
Liam: cost note: cross-region routing added ~0.9TB egress to us-east this hour — that's ~$700 on top of normal. We should include cost impact in the postmortem.
infra-bot: Deploy bot: geo-dns-config v2.7 rolled back -> v2.6 at 1779991342 by Liam. Action: create canary for prefer_same_continent policy.
Arjun: next steps — 1) make NAT scaling autoscale based on active NAT ports, 2) add EDNS/EDNS-client-subnet awareness to GeoDNS to avoid wrong netmapping, 3) test fallback policy in chaos env. I'll draft RFC.
Sophia: +1 on chaos test. Also add a rate limiter on long-lived streaming sessions per-LB to avoid single-host pinning.
Maya: I'm drafting the incident note and will include timeline + commands used: `gcloud compute addresses create eu-nat-pool-ephem --addresses=...` and LB drain steps. Will ping infra on review.
Liam: nice. We'll run postmortem after everyone's comments. Thanks all :thumbsup:
